subject: Ping: intermittent WebSocket stall during high-concurrency demo - Zenith Health
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@zenithhealth.com>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng-ops@zenithhealth.com
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo run — repeated silent output / websocket timeouts

Mateo,

We just ran the scheduled demo against the sandbox cluster and hit multiple instances where the WebSocket stream would silence for ~6–12s mid-response. This happened when we pushed concurrent sessions (approx 140 concurrent users) and while token throughput was high. The UI shows partial responses (chunks) then nothing — the session doesn't close but no further chunks arrive until a long pause.

Attached a small bundle (logs_chunk_20271102.tar.gz) with the client-side websocket trace + the agent-side traces (we redacted PII). Also included websocket_trace_20271102.json with sequence numbers.

We need this investigated urgently — this happened in front of stakeholders. Can you confirm whether this is a client-side retry/backoff or a server-side stall? We are at risk of delaying rollout if this recurs in the next staging pass.

Thanks,
Sofia Ramos
Director, Product — Zenith Health

---
Attachment: logs_chunk_20271102.tar.gz (application/gzip, 2.1MB)
Attachment: websocket_trace_20271102.json (application/json, 240KB)
From: mateo_alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@zenithhealth.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 16:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo run — repeated silent output / websocket timeouts

Thanks for the traces and the quick heads-up, Sofia — sorry you hit this during the demo. I'm looped into Engineering and we're standing up a short investigation. Initial notes:

- From the client trace the socket remained open (no FIN) but server-side token emission stops.
- The sequence numbers in websocket_trace_20271102.json indicate missing chunk ranges (gap at tokens 1200–1224) that line up with the pause you saw.

Evelyn and Jordan, can one of you triage the server-side logs for the model-host process on the 2027-11-02 23:40–23:50 UTC window (approx). If this is on our end we need a hotfix; if it’s backpressure from Zenith’s edge or a middlebox, we need to confirm.

Sofia — I suggest we set a 30-minute bridge now so we can share screens and go through the traces. Are you available at 17:15 PST?

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@zenithhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo run — repeated silent output / websocket timeouts

On Tue, Nov 2, 2027 at 4:38 PM Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Evelyn and Jordan, can one of you triage the server-side logs for the model-host process on the 2027-11-02 23:40–23:50 UTC window (approx). If this is on our end we need a hotfix; if it’s backpressure from Zenith’s edge or a middlebox, we need to confirm.

Quick update from infra triage: we see a burst of concurrent requests that caused an uneven scheduling spike on the GPU-backed host pool (host-7c4). During the spike the inference runtime deferred kernel selection for a small set of containers, resulting in stalled token emission for ~6–10s in 7 separate sessions.

Action plan (short):
- Temporarily route Zenith traffic to host pool-accelerated (hot) lane to avoid the late-stage scheduling path (will increase cost but reduces scheduling jitter).
- Add a temporary per-tenant concurrency cap at 100 to keep the scheduling path stable while we patch the kernel selection path.
- Create STREAM-948 referencing a deterministic replay of the traces for the runtime team.

We can effect the routing change now and then rollback after the staged patch.

Evelyn Hart
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Caleb Turner <caleb.turner@zenithhealth.com>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@zenithhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 01:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Demo run — repeated silent output / websocket timeouts

Appreciate the quick digs. This is serious for us — we had a meeting with compliance and they want confirmation that the live demo path meets our latency targets under expected concurrency. We cannot accept intermittent 6–12s stalls.

Two asks: can you provide a short-term mitigation that we can validate in the next hour (routing to a hot lane + concurrency cap is fine), and can you commit to a timeline for a code-level fix (we need a patch or rollback plan this week)? Also, include any observable metrics we can share with our stakeholders (per-session stall counts, host IDs, timestamps).

If you want to open a support escalation ticket (priority: Sev-2), please do so and share the incident link.

— Caleb Turner
VP Product Operations — Zenith Health
From: mateo_alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
To: evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@zenithhealth.com>, Caleb Turner <caleb.turner@zenithhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo run — repeated silent output / websocket timeouts — (exec status + action plan)

Status update and next steps: we executed the short-term mitigations at 08:20 UTC (route => hot lane + per-tenant concurrency cap = 100). Preliminary validation shows no silent-chunk stalls in the next 90 minutes across the same synthetic load used by Zenith.

Immediate deliverables:
- Hot lane routing active (host pool: hot-accelerated).
- Temporary concurrency cap: 100 per tenant (config change id: cfg-7821).
- Replayed traces to runtime team and opened JIRA STREAM-948 (https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/STREAM-948).
- ETA for code-level fix: runtime team targeting a canary patch by 2027-11-05 and cluster-wide rollout by 2027-11-09, barring regressions.
- Incident ticket created: INC-20271103-WS (internal) and we will attach per-session stall counts + host IDs.

We will continue to monitor the customer’s staging cluster and I will schedule a 30-minute sync at 11:00 PST to review metrics and confirm the demo path.

Thanks for the rapid escalation everyone.

— Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
